preamble: Those with 2, 4, 5 down, 7, 16 down 26, and 22s are probably 1 down 19 and can be 6-d. Clues to these mostly lack definition.

clue.text: Copper is inserted in a drain in church

indicators.note: what is inserted is pushed inside something else, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a copper is a policeman, a PC (police constable)

explanation.surface: A police officer gets stuck in a church drain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' wants to be the metal, Cu, but it is the policeman; a PC is a police constable in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A piscina is the stone basin near a church altar with an outlet for rinsing the sacred vessels.

clue.text: The captive monarch: she's kept in a mount

parts.note: a captive is a prisoner of war, POW

indicators.note: something kept in a place is held inside it, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: a steed is a horse to ride
'she' points back to the monarch, so ER again

explanation.surface: A queen held prisoner is put up on a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble supplies the meaning: this is one of the car features. 'She' points back to the monarch, so the same royal abbreviation is used twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Per the preamble, cars with these features are probably power steered, steering assisted by a hydraulic or electric motor.

clue.text: Number 4's out of order

indicators.note: things out of order are not in their proper sequence, so the letters must be rearranged

parts.note: NO is the abbreviation for number
the digit written as a word

explanation.surface: Something numbered four is broken.
explanation.walkthrough: '4' looks like a cross-reference to 4 down, but here it is just the word FOUR. The preamble gives the meaning: a car feature.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunroof is a panel in a car's roof that opens to let in light and air, one of the preamble's car extras.

clue.text: Unreliable for a brief moment when leaderless

indicators.note: without a leader means without the front, so the opening letter goes

parts.note: a jiffy is a very short time

explanation.surface: Something proves untrustworthy for a moment after losing its chief.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the J from JIFFY to get IFFY.
explanation.definitionFit: Iffy is informal for doubtful or of questionable quality, which is what something unreliable is.

clue.text: State in exposure

indicators.note: being in something means lying inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: an airing is an exposure to the open air or to public view

explanation.surface: A country lies open to view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a nation, but it means condition. The preamble supplies the meaning: a car feature.
explanation.definitionFit: Air-conditioning cools and dries the air inside a car's cabin, one of the preamble's listed car extras.

clue.text: Excavation into unusual heap in the cemetery

indicators.note: going into something means entering it, so one piece is placed inside another
something unusual is not in its normal form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a pit is a hole dug out

explanation.surface: Digging into an odd mound in a graveyard.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: an epitaph is something found in the cemetery, carved on a tombstone. The dug pit and heap make the surface feel like gravedigging.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitaph is the inscription on a gravestone, so it is what one reads among the graves of a burial ground.

clue.text: Choose endlessly well-to-do former partners without name

indicators.note: with no end means the final letter is dropped
without in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Pick the rich ex-spouses who have no name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' here means outside, not lacking, so the name goes inside the former partners. The preamble gives the meaning: a car feature.
explanation.definitionFit: Electric windows are car windows raised and lowered by a motor at the press of a button, one of the preamble's extras.

clue.text: Stop the crowd within roughly two miles

indicators.note: within means inside, so one piece sits inside another
roughly means not exactly, so these letters come in an inexact order

explanation.surface: Halting a crowd about two miles away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two miles' looks like a distance, but the two is Roman II joining the letters of MILES for rearranging. The preamble also counts an immobiliser among the car features.
explanation.definitionFit: To immobilise something is to prevent it moving, bringing it to a halt; a car immobiliser halts thieves.

clue.text: The atmosphere is captivating

parts.note: to bag is to capture, so it bags

explanation.surface: The mood is enchanting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Captivating' reads as charming, but it means capturing, as a hunter bags game. The preamble supplies the meaning: a car feature.
explanation.definitionFit: Airbags are cushions that inflate instantly in a crash to protect a car's occupants, one of the preamble's extras.

clue.text: It's two thirds empty and lies low

definitions.note: a verb phrase describing the country, which 'It' stands for

indicators.note: keeping two thirds means the last third is cut away

parts.note: hollow, of which only four of six letters are kept

explanation.surface: Something mostly hollow that sits low down.
explanation.walkthrough: HOLLOW loses its last third, OW, leaving HOLL. The definition describes the country: much of it lies below sea level.
explanation.definitionFit: Holland, the Netherlands, is famously low-lying, with large areas reclaimed from the sea behind dykes.

clue.text: Show pain about number in favour measured by Beaufort

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: to wince is to flinch in pain
to be for something is to favour it

explanation.surface: Flinching about some figure judged on a weather scale.
explanation.walkthrough: The Beaufort scale, devised by Admiral Beaufort, rates winds from 0 (calm) to 12 (hurricane).
explanation.definitionFit: The Beaufort scale grades the strength of wind, so wind force is what it measures.

clue.text: Possible sequel to extra painting

parts.note: extramural, so this ending can follow extra

explanation.surface: A follow-up to a bonus picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extra' is not a bonus but the start of a word: extramural, meaning outside the walls of a university, is completed by this word.
explanation.definitionFit: A mural is a picture painted directly onto a wall, so it is a kind of painting.

clue.text: One that has got into corruption causes disturbance

indicators.note: getting into something means ending up inside it

explanation.surface: Someone drawn into graft stirs up trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One that' is the Roman I, and 'causes' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A riot is a violent public disturbance by a crowd, a breach of the peace.

clue.text: Charge a supporter opposed to a holiday area

parts.note: a bra is a supporting garment

explanation.surface: Accusing a fan of objecting to a resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter' looks like a fan; in crosswords it is often the bra. V is versus, as in a fixture list.
explanation.definitionFit: The Costa Brava is the Catalan coast of north-east Spain, a popular resort region for package tourists.

clue.text: Premier musician keeps one ward diverted

indicators.note: something diverted is sent off its course, so these letters are rerouted into a new order

explanation.surface: A star performer looks after a hospital patient who has been sent elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeps' looks like a verb but is just letters. Ignacy Paderewski was a celebrated pianist who became Prime Minister of Poland in 1919.
explanation.definitionFit: Paderewski was both a concert pianist and his country's prime minister, so he was literally a premier and a musician.

clue.text: Far off assistance, I'm sorry to say

definitions.note: the answer replaces 'sorry to say' in the phrase 'I'm afraid'

indicators.note: off means not right, as food goes off, so these letters are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Apologising that help is a long way away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Far off' reads as distant, but 'off' is the signal to rearrange FAR.
explanation.definitionFit: 'I'm afraid' is a polite formula of regret, the same as saying 'I'm sorry to say' before bad news.

clue.text: Some pictures are (by a journalist) exploited

explanation.surface: Photographs taken by a reporter have been misused.
explanation.walkthrough: The brackets make the journalist look like an aside, but the editor is part of the wordplay; 'Some pictures' is the abbreviation for illustrations.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ill-used has been treated badly or taken advantage of, the same as being exploited.

clue.text: Fellow-worker is compelling without one

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps around another

explanation.surface: A colleague is persuasive even when working alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but it means outside: COGENT goes around A.
explanation.definitionFit: A co-agent is someone acting jointly with another, a colleague sharing the same work or task.

clue.text: Little money to get hold of when backing a sovereign

parts.note: a cent is a small coin

indicators.note: backing means moving in reverse, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: to collar someone is to seize them

explanation.surface: A small sum to grab while betting on a gold coin.
explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign is also an old British gold coin, which fits the money picture, but here it is the king. The preamble supplies the meaning: a car feature.
explanation.definitionFit: Central locking secures all of a car's doors at once from a single key or switch, one of the preamble's extras.

clue.text: People of intelligence about to hole up for a way of keeping fit

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective, as in aerobic exercise

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from bottom to top
about means around, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: the Central Intelligence Agency, the US spy service
to bore is to drill a hole

explanation.surface: Spies going into hiding while staying in shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hole up' looks like hiding; split it, so 'to hole' is the drilling verb and 'up' tells a down answer to read from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerobic exercise raises the heart rate and oxygen use; aerobics is a popular fitness routine.

clue.text: No.1 sage is in point

indicators.note: being in something means lying inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: west is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: The top wise man has a point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point' is a compass point, W, E, N or S, here in full; and 'No.1 sage' is used adjectivally as the most sage.
explanation.definitionFit: Sage as an adjective means wise, so the number one, most sage, is the superlative of wise.

clue.text: See 1
Dogfish (look after dog) shunned our treatment

parts.note: to nurse is to care for
a second route: the letters of the first two words rearranged also make the answer

explanation.surface: A fish that refused our care.
explanation.walkthrough: Two routes to one answer: the bracketed charade, and 'shunned our' rearranged, with 'treatment' as the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The nursehound is a large spotted catshark of European waters, a kind of dogfish.

clue.text: Very considerable backing for a stone

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: a gem is a precious stone

explanation.surface: Huge support for a jewel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' looks like support, but it signals reading backwards. 'Stone' is not a weight here but a gem.
explanation.definitionFit: Mega is informal slang for huge or enormous, so it means very considerable.

clue.text: Love in a friend isn't pure

definitions.note: a verb phrase; the answer is the thing that is not pure

indicators.note: being in something means lying inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: Loving a friend is not an innocent thing.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble's 22s are alloy wheels on a car, but this clue has its own definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An alloy is a mixture of metals, so by nature it is not a pure single element.

clue.text: A friend much wronged?

indicators.note: something wronged is badly treated, so these letters are knocked out of shape

explanation.surface: A pal who has been badly treated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Much wronged' reads as a phrase about suffering; MUCH is the letters and 'wronged' the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Chum is a familiar British word for a close companion or pal.

clue.text: Confederate (American) making visual pun

parts.note: a Reb was a Confederate soldier in the American Civil War

explanation.surface: A Southern soldier comes up with a picture joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Johnny Reb' was the Union nickname for a Confederate soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebus is a puzzle representing words by pictures and letters, a pun conveyed by images.

clue.text: Is different on a line where summers are similar

definitions.note: an adverbial clause; the answer is an adjective, said of such a line

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Things vary along a boundary where summers match.
explanation.walkthrough: The line in the wordplay is also the map line the definition describes.
explanation.definitionFit: An isotheral line on a map joins places having the same mean summer temperature.

clue.text: See 16 down
When my prince will come in the form of a samoyed

indicators.note: taking a form means being reshaped, so these letters are remade into a new order

parts.note: the dog breed, its letters to be rearranged; the 'a' only completes the phrase

explanation.surface: A fairytale prince arrives as a fluffy white dog.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition completes the Snow White song 'Some Day My Prince Will Come'. A samoyed is a white Siberian sledge dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The Disney song title gives the answer: the time when the prince will come is at some unspecified future time.
